newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Central Bank considers issuing leu CDs.
newsitem.headline: Romania Central Bank considers issuing leu CDs.

text.p: Romania's Central Bank (BNR) is considering issuing certificates of deposit in its own name to soak up excessive liquidity in the national leu currency, an adviser to the bank governor said on Sunday.
Teodor Buftea told a news conference after a cabinet meeting that the bank had not yet taken a final decision on the certificates.
He said the bank had purchased an average of $20 million per day in recent months, helping to build up reserves, which reached $1.45 billion at the end of last month.
The purchases followed an excess of dollars on the market triggered by foreign capital inflows and were aimed at preventing a sharp appreciation of the leu, which might hurt Romanian exporters.
The leu has staged a strong recovery in the last two months, stabilising at about 7,100 to the dollar after sliding to a record low of 9,000 in mid-February.

The money market in recent weeks has been liquid with short-term prices dropping to 95 percent from about 190 percent at the beginning of April. The BNR seeks to maintain interest rate levels at positive real terms.
Monthly inflation slowed to 6.9 percent in April from a record 30.7 percent the previous month.
The proposed issue is part of the BNR's intention of introducing open-market operations as its main instrument of conducting its monetary policy.
